There are three exported ops. They all run the permission check before anything is written, using `chatGate` (`apps/server/src/sync/ops.ts:268`). `chatGate` loads the actor's grants and the chat's placement once, in parallel, and returns a function that throws `Forbidden` if `can()` says no. When an op asks more than one question, every answer comes from that same snapshot. | Op | Checks before writing | Then writes | |---|---|---| | `send` (`ops.ts:82`) | `post` on the chat | Inside `applyOnce`: allocates an ordinal and a revision, inserts the message, bumps `spaces.last_activity_at`, appends a `message.created` event | | `deleteMessage` (`ops.ts:171`) | 1. `read` on the chat, before the message is looked up, so a non-member can't find out whether a message exists
2. The message exists and belongs to this chat, otherwise `MessageNotFoundError`
3. `delete_own` if the actor wrote it, otherwise `delete_any` (moderation, granted at the space level) | Inside `applyOnce`: allocates a revision but no ordinal, clears the body and sets `deleted`, appends a `message.deleted` event | | `markRead` (`ops.ts:243`) | `read` on the chat | Upserts `chat_read_state` using `GREATEST`, so a stale device can't move the cursor backwards. There's no ledger entry and no revision, because repeating it changes nothing | `MessageNotFoundError` is also exported, but it's an error class, not an op. A few things the code doesn't check: - **Permission checks run before `applyOnce`, including on retries.** A retried `send` or `deleteMessage` checks permissions again before the ledger can return the stored ack. If the actor lost access in between, the retry throws `Forbidden` even though the original write went through. - **`send` only checks `post`.** It doesn't confirm that `parentId` exists or belongs to the same chat. If anything enforces that, it's a database constraint, not this file. - **`markRead` accepts any `ord`.** It doesn't check the value against the chat's highest ordinal, so a client can move its cursor past the last message. - **Deleting a message that's already deleted isn't short-circuited.** It allocates a new revision anyway, and the doc comment says this is on purpose.
